title: Cron sweeps: deterministic selection, Workflow-enforced budgets
description:
D14/D15. A schedule picks work and runs it without anyone asking.

TWO PROPERTIES THE DESIGN DOC IS EXPLICIT ABOUT, and both are about auditability rather than capability:
- SELECTION IS DETERMINISTIC: priority, then age, then id. No model call, no judgement. 'Why did it pick these five' must have a boring answer.
- BUDGETS ARE ENFORCED BY THE WORKFLOW, not by the prompt (D14). Phase 2 established what happens otherwise — a run that outlives its supervisor keeps spending, and the record it writes cannot report its own death.

The sweep policy shape from the design doc: a filter, max_ticks, budget_usd, tier and a completion gate. Phase 2's clamp lesson applies to every one of those numbers: report the EFFECTIVE budget after clamping, because an operator whose ceiling was silently replaced learns about it from a cancelled run.
acceptance_criteria: A cron sweep selects deterministically and the selection is explainable from the record alone; its budget is enforced by the Workflow and the effective value is reported; a sweep that trips its budget stops without losing the work already done.
